code: torch_available <- requireNamespace("torch", quietly = TRUE) &&   isTRUE(tryCatch(torch::torch_is_installed(), error = function(e) FALSE)) torch_available #> [1] FALSE set.seed(1) data_fit_masked <- data_fit_all[[1]] n <- nrow(data_fit_masked) data_fit_masked$serBilir[sample.int(n, floor(0.12 * n))] <- NA data_fit_masked$albumin[sample.int(n, floor(0.12 * n))] <- NA imputed <- imputeLongitudinal(   data_fit_masked, long_sub_fixed, long_sub_random,   time_variable = "year", epochs = 80, seed = 1 ) imputed$diagnostics$serBilir count_retained <- function(data_fit_all, long_sub_fixed, id = "id") {   if (is.data.frame(data_fit_all)) {     data_fit_all <- rep(list(data_fit_all), length(long_sub_fixed))   }   ids_by_marker <- lapply(seq_along(long_sub_fixed), function(m) {     d <- data_fit_all[[m]]     complete <- d[rowSums(is.na(d[all.vars(long_sub_fixed[[m]])])) == 0, ]     unique(complete[[id]])   })   Reduce(intersect, ids_by_marker) }  length(count_retained(data_fit_masked, long_sub_fixed)) length(count_retained(imputed$data_fit_all, long_sub_fixed)) long_fit_imputed <- longitudinalSub(imputed$data_fit_all, long_sub_fixed, long_sub_random)

what: Step 3: Predict event risk with predictRisk()
title: Getting started with BJM
text: predict specific patient, build data_predict_all list (one data.frame per biomarker, mirroring data_fit_all) containing patient’s measurements prediction_time — later measurements available yet real prediction setting. predict, patient 2, risk event type within one year year = 5. survival_variable_all/survival_trans_function describe raw event-time variable transformed integration grid; see ?predictRisk details. survival_variable_all/survival_trans_function almost always follow convention shown : variables named "Tyears1", "Tyears2", …, absolute distance fixed cut point. survivalTrans() builds exactly pair plain vector cut points, hand-write two matching parallel lists: risk_prob_1 risk_prob_2 predicted probabilities experiencing two competing event types within one-year horizon, conditional patient’s longitudinal history survival prediction_time. (risk_prob_2 NULL whenever survival_fit_all fit without form_conditional_cr.)
code: survival_variable_all <- list("Tyears1", "Tyears2", "Tyears3", "Tyears4") survival_trans_function <- list(   fun1 = function(x) abs(x - 1),   fun2 = function(x) abs(x - 3),   fun3 = function(x) abs(x - 5),   fun4 = function(x) abs(x - 7) )  data_raw_predict <- pbc3[pbc3$id == 2 & pbc3$year <= 5, ] data_predict_all <- list(data_raw_predict, data_raw_predict)  risk <- predictRisk(   data_predict_all, long_fit_all, survival_fit_all,   prediction_time = 5, horizon = 1, time_variable = "year",   survival_variable_all, survival_trans_function,   bandcount1 = 10, bandcount2 = 20 )  risk #>  #> ================================================================= #>  Dynamic Prediction - Event Risk #> ----------------------------------------------------------------- #>   Competing risks   : Yes #>   Subjects          : 1 #> ----------------------------------------------------------------- #>  #>  Subject Cause 1 Risk Cause 2 Risk Total Risk #>        2       0.0377       0.0017     0.0393 #>  #> ================================================================= trans <- survivalTrans(c(1, 3, 5, 7)) identical(trans$survival_variable_all, survival_variable_all) #> [1] TRUE trans$survival_trans_function[[1]](2) #> [1] 1

what: Step 4: Predict a future biomarker value with predictLongitudinal()
title: Getting started with BJM
text: predictLongitudinal() answers different question: whether event happens, specific biomarker’s value likely prediction_time + horizon, conditional survival time. bio_i selects biomarker(s) position long_fit_all (1 = serBilir ); naming exactly one biomarker returns single result, naming one (leaving bio_i = NULL every biomarker) returns named list results instead, computing shared, bio_i-independent part pipeline reusing across every biomarker. Y_predict MAP (likely) predicted value; Y_density/Y_all give full predicted density grid candidate values, predictPlot() visualizes (see ?predictPlot).
code: bio_pred <- predictLongitudinal(   bio_i = 1, data_predict_all, long_fit_all, survival_fit_all,   prediction_time = 5, horizon = 1, time_variable = "year",   survival_variable_all, survival_trans_function,   bandcount2 = 20, bandcount3 = 50 )  bio_pred$Y_predict #>        2  #> 1.193408

text: ?predictPlot ?riskPlot visualize outputs predictLongitudinal()/predictRisk() single patient. ?cmtPlot plots observed longitudinal trajectories stratified eventual outcome, useful checking whether biomarker looks informative fitting. ?spaghettiPlot draws subject’s observed trajectory, optionally aligned event time, ?cifPlot plots cumulative incidence (competing) event type. ?performancePlot evaluates risk predictions (time-dependent AUC Brier score) across landmark times, ideally held-data, ?calibrationPlot compares predicted observed risks. ?imputeLongitudinal fills missing longitudinal biomarker values due interrupted follow-longitudinalSub() runs, instead relying complete-case analysis (see “Optional: imputing interrupted follow-fitting” ). ?poolLongitudinalSub combines longitudinalSub() fits across multiple completed datasets imputeLongitudinal(..., impute = "multiple") Rubin’s rules, imputation uncertainty reflected reported standard errors (see “Propagating imputation uncertainty poolLongitudinalSub()” ).

what: A twin that is updated at each visit
title: Digital twins
text: Patient 2 followed 14 years. build twin three times, years 1, 3 5, time measurements taken far, draw 500 futures next five years. event time type set NA: times known yet. simulateTrajectory() returns one row per draw time, summary lines ordinary R. draw’s event time repeated rows; keeping first row draw gives one row per future. twin’s risk event within three years grows patient’s bilirubin rises: forecast bilirubin, every measurement patient actually . Filled points ones twin built ; open points measured later, show twin’s forecasts compare happened.  plot(sims) plot(sims, = "event") draw single twin directly; see Plotting BJM.
code: patient <- pbc3[pbc3$id == 2, ]  twin_at <- function(landmark) {   history <- patient[patient$year <= landmark, ]   history$years <- NA   history$status4 <- NA   sims <- simulateTrajectory(history, long_fit_all, survival_fit_all,                              prediction_time = landmark,                              times = seq(landmark, landmark + 5, by = 0.25),                              time_variable = "year",                              trans$survival_variable_all, trans$survival_trans_function,                              n_sim = 500, seed = 1)   sims$landmark <- landmark   as.data.frame(sims) } twins <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(1, 3, 5), twin_at)) futures <- twins[!duplicated(twins[c("landmark", "sim")]), ] aggregate(cbind(risk_3_years = event == 1 & event_time <= landmark + 3) ~ landmark,           data = futures, FUN = mean) #>   landmark risk_3_years #> 1        1        0.036 #> 2        3        0.102 #> 3        5        0.212 bands <- aggregate(serBilir ~ landmark + year, data = twins,                    FUN = function(v) quantile(v, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))) bands <- do.call(data.frame, bands) names(bands)[3:5] <- c("lower", "median", "upper")  measured <- merge(patient[c("year", "serBilir")], data.frame(landmark = c(1, 3, 5))) measured$used <- ifelse(measured$year <= measured$landmark, "used by the twin", "measured later")  ggplot(bands, aes(x = year)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "#2166AC", alpha = 0.2) +   geom_line(aes(y = median), color = "#2166AC", linewidth = 1) +   geom_point(data = measured, aes(y = serBilir, shape = used), size = 2) +   scale_shape_manual(values = c("used by the twin" = 16, "measured later" = 1), name = NULL) +   geom_vline(aes(xintercept = landmark), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +   facet_wrap(~ landmark, labeller = label_both) +   ylab("serBilir") + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

code: virtual <- data.frame(id = c("age 40", "age 70"), year = 0, age = c(40, 70), sex = 1,                       serBilir = NA, albumin = NA) virtual_sims <- simulateTrajectory(virtual, long_fit_all, survival_fit_all,                                    prediction_time = 0, times = 0:10, time_variable = "year",                                    trans$survival_variable_all, trans$survival_trans_function,                                    n_sim = 1000, seed = 1) virtual_futures <- virtual_sims[!duplicated(virtual_sims[c("id", "sim")]), ] aggregate(cbind(death_5_years = event == 1 & status4 == 0 & event_time <= 5,                 transplant_5_years = event == 1 & status4 == 1 & event_time <= 5,                 event_free_14_years = event == 0) ~ id,           data = virtual_futures, FUN = mean) #>       id death_5_years transplant_5_years event_free_14_years #> 1 age 40         0.167              0.109               0.387 #> 2 age 70         0.420              0.002               0.207 grid <- seq(0, attr(virtual_sims, "max_event_time"), length.out = 200) incidence <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(virtual_futures, virtual_futures$id), function(d) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(c(death = 0, transplantation = 1), function(type) {     data.frame(id = d$id[1], time = grid,                event = if (type == 0) "death" else "transplantation",                incidence = vapply(grid, function(t)                  mean(d$event == 1 & d$status4 == type & d$event_time <= t), numeric(1)))   })) }))  ggplot(incidence, aes(x = time, y = incidence, color = id)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   facet_wrap(~ event) +   labs(x = "year", y = "Cumulative incidence", color = NULL) +   theme_bw()

code: simulate_study <- function(n, seed) {   set.seed(seed)   x <- rnorm(n)   T <- (-log(runif(n)) / (0.05 * exp(0.5 * x)))^(1 / 1.5)   # true_T is kept only to check the methods below; a real study does not have it   surv <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n), x = x, L = NA_real_, R = NA_real_, true_T = T)   long <- vector("list", n)   for (i in seq_len(n)) {     visits <- c(0, cumsum(runif(20, 1, 3)))     visits <- visits[visits < runif(1, 4, 15)]     if (T[i] > max(visits)) {                 # not detected: right-censored       surv$L[i] <- max(visits)       seen <- visits     } else {                                  # detected at the next visit       k <- findInterval(T[i], visits)       surv$L[i] <- visits[k]       surv$R[i] <- visits[k + 1]       seen <- visits[visits <= T[i]]     }     b <- rnorm(2, 0, c(0.5, 0.1))     long[[i]] <- data.frame(id = i, year = seen, x = x[i],                             y = 1 + 0.3 * seen - 0.2 * T[i] + 0.4 * x[i] +                               b[1] + b[2] * seen + rnorm(length(seen), 0, 0.3))   }   list(surv = surv, long = do.call(rbind, long)) } study <- simulate_study(300, seed = 1) head(study$surv) #>   id          x        L        R     true_T #> 1  1 -0.6264538 2.663798 5.197483  3.1615219 #> 2  2  0.1836433 0.000000 1.856694  1.2203314 #> 3  3 -0.8356286 4.142883       NA 15.0069579 #> 4  4  1.5952808 1.656316 4.656177  1.8876750 #> 5  5  0.3295078 0.000000 2.753717  0.5590590 #> 6  6 -0.8204684 0.000000 2.003273  0.8397886 head(study$long) #>   id     year          x          y #> 1  1 0.000000 -0.6264538  1.3414335 #> 2  1 2.663798 -0.6264538  1.2273575 #> 3  2 0.000000  0.1836433  0.2401363 #> 4  3 0.000000 -0.8356286 -2.4914256 #> 5  3 2.767505 -0.8356286 -1.2055779 #> 6  3 4.142883 -0.8356286 -0.6163481

Its #> basis/contrasts depend on the data it is computed from, and for this formula #> BJM rebuilds the design matrix from the data at hand (a single patient's rows #> at prediction time) instead of reusing the training-time basis -- so this can #> silently produce incorrect predictions, or fail outright when there are too few #> distinct values. title: Recurrent events
text: BJM ship recurrent-event data set, simulate small cohort shape data . code makes example data; skip next section . need two tables. events: one row per readmission, death end follow-. time event happened, status 1 readmission, 2 death 0 end follow-nothing happening, discharge stay readmission began ends (NA stay: death, follow-ending). columns covariates. labs: one row per measurement, time axis. Times 0 labs first hospital stay. picture shows one patient’s data looks like cut episodes.
code: # One patient: time-to-readmission and type depend on age, sex, the number of # previous readmissions and a patient-level frailty; a biomarker's trajectory # in each episode depends on how long that episode lasts. Times are in months # since the first (index) discharge. simulate_patient <- function(id, follow_up = c(6, 12), max_episodes = 12) {   age <- rnorm(1, 70, 8); sex <- rbinom(1, 1, 0.5); age_c <- (age - 70) / 10   frailty <- rnorm(1, 0, 0.5)   u0 <- rnorm(1, 0, 0.5) + 0.8 * frailty; u1 <- rnorm(1, 0, 0.3)   end_of_follow_up <- if (is.null(follow_up)) Inf else runif(1, follow_up[1], follow_up[2])   stay <- function() max(0.08, rexp(1, 1 / 0.25))        # months in hospital    start <- 0; stay_before <- stay(); k <- 0   events <- list(); labs <- list(); starts <- numeric(0)   repeat {     k <- k + 1; starts[k] <- start     gap <- (-log(runif(1)) / (0.25 * exp(0.3 * age_c + 0.3 * sex + 0.25 * (k - 1) + frailty)))^(1 / 1.2)     dies <- rbinom(1, 1, plogis(-2 + 0.5 * gap + 0.3 * age_c + 0.3 * (k - 1)))     end <- start + gap     censored <- end > end_of_follow_up     stop_time <- if (censored) end_of_follow_up else end      # labs: two in the stay before this discharge, one at discharge, then     # a visit every half month while the patient is still at risk     t <- c(start - stay_before * c(0.7, 0.3), start)     j <- 1     while (start + 0.5 * j < stop_time) { t <- c(t, start + 0.5 * j); j <- j + 1 }     mean_lab <- 5 + u0 + (-0.3 + u1) * (t - start) + 0.4 * gap - 0.5 * gap * (t - start) +       0.05 * age_c + 0.2 * sex     labs[[k]] <- data.frame(id = id, t = t, biomarker = rnorm(length(t), mean_lab, 0.4))      row <- function(time, status, discharge = NA_real_)       data.frame(id = id, time = time, status = status, discharge = discharge, age = age, sex = sex)     if (censored) { events[[k]] <- row(end_of_follow_up, 0L); break }     if (dies == 1) { events[[k]] <- row(end, 2L); break }     next_stay <- stay()     events[[k]] <- row(end, 1L, discharge = end + next_stay)     if (end + next_stay >= end_of_follow_up || k >= max_episodes) break     start <- end + next_stay; stay_before <- next_stay   }   list(events = do.call(rbind, events), labs = do.call(rbind, labs), starts = starts) }  cohort <- lapply(1:300, simulate_patient) events <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cohort, `[[`, "events")) labs   <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cohort, `[[`, "labs")) head(events[events$id == 1, ], 5) #>   id     time status discharge      age sex #> 1  1 1.575685      1  2.043283 74.16471   0 #> 2  1 4.711596      1  5.309283 74.16471   0 #> 3  1 9.484838      0        NA 74.16471   0 head(labs[labs$id == 1, ], 5) #>   id          t biomarker #> 1  1 -0.9399152  5.574503 #> 2  1 -0.4028208  4.606169 #> 3  1  0.0000000  3.231357 #> 4  1  0.5000000  3.219372 #> 5  1  1.0000000  3.522247

code: history_at_discharge <- function(p, k) {   now <- p$starts[k]   ev <- p$events[seq_len(k - 1), ]                       # earlier readmissions   last <- data.frame(id = p$events$id[1], time = now + 0.001, status = 0L, discharge = NA_real_,                      age = p$events$age[1], sex = p$events$sex[1])   list(events = rbind(ev, last), labs = p$labs[p$labs$t <= now, ]) }  set.seed(7) fresh <- lapply(5001:5040, simulate_patient, follow_up = NULL) reach2 <- Filter(function(p) length(p$starts) >= 2, fresh)      # patients with a 2nd discharge chosen <- list(   list(p = fresh[[1]], k = 1), list(p = fresh[[2]], k = 1), list(p = reach2[[1]], k = 2)) histories <- lapply(chosen, function(x) history_at_discharge(x$p, x$k)) for (i in seq_along(histories)) {                        # give each prediction its own id   histories[[i]]$events$id <- histories[[i]]$labs$id <- 9000 + i } now_events <- do.call(rbind, lapply(histories, `[[`, "events")) now_labs   <- do.call(rbind, lapply(histories, `[[`, "labs"))  now <- buildRecurrentEpisodes(now_events, now_labs, time_variable_long = "t",                               restart_variable = "discharge", lookback = Inf) # each patient's last episode is the one still open open <- now$long_data[now$long_data$episode == ave(now$long_data$episode, now$long_data$id, FUN = max), ] head(open[, c("episode_id", "t", "time_in_episode", "gap", "biomarker", "event_type")], 4) #>   episode_id           t time_in_episode gap biomarker event_type #> 1     9001:1 -0.14213393     -0.14213393  NA  5.387458         NA #> 2     9001:1 -0.06091454     -0.06091454  NA  5.468732         NA #> 3     9001:1  0.00000000      0.00000000  NA  6.263731         NA #> 4     9002:1 -0.05600000     -0.05600000  NA  5.488383         NA

text: BJM fits backward joint model multivariate longitudinal outcomes time--event data, uses make dynamic predictions: given patient’s longitudinal history prediction_time, predict risk event (, desired, future biomarker values) conditional survival point. backward joint model formulation keeps fitting prediction fast, even large sample sizes many longitudinal variables, accommodates irregularly measured longitudinal data competing risks.

title: Backward Joint Model for the Dynamic Prediction of Both Time-to-Event and Longitudinal Outcomes
text: Fitting prediction four-step pipeline: fit survival sub-model, fit longitudinal sub-model per biomarker, combine predict event risk /future biomarker values. survival_variable_all/survival_trans_function follow common convention ("Tyears1", "Tyears2", …, absolute distance fixed cut point); survivalTrans(c(1, 3, 5, 7)) builds pair instead hand-writing two matching lists. every data_*_all argument shown (data_fit_all, data_predict_all, …) also accepts single bare data.frame — reused every biomarker — instead repeated list, biomarkers share measurement data. predictPlot() riskPlot() visualize predictions single patient; cmtPlot() plots observed longitudinal trajectories stratified eventual outcome, spaghettiPlot() draws every subject’s trajectory (optionally aligned event time), cifPlot() plots cumulative incidence event type. plot() works fitted sub-models predictLongitudinal() results, model diagnostics predicted biomarker distributions, performancePlot() plots time-dependent AUC Brier score risk predictions across landmark times, calibrationPlot() compares predicted observed risks. full walkthrough — including choose bandcount1/ bandcount2/bandcount3 numerical-integration tuning parameters via convergence check, input-validation error messages look like — see vignette("BJM-intro", package = "BJM").
code: library(BJM) data(pbc3)  ## 1. Fit the survival sub-model (one row per patient) data_survival_fitting <- pbc3[!duplicated(pbc3$id), ]  survival_fit_all <- survivalSub(   data_survival_fitting,   form_marginal_surv = Surv(years, status3) ~ age + sex,   form_conditional_cr = status4 ~ years + age + sex )  ## 2. Fit the longitudinal sub-model(s), one per biomarker long_sub_fixed <- list(   "serBilir" = serBilir ~ year + age + sex + (years) + (years) * year,   "albumin"  = albumin  ~ year + age + sex + (years) + (years) * year ) long_sub_random <- list(   "serBilir" = ~ year | id,   "albumin"  = ~ year | id ) data_fit_all <- list(pbc3[pbc3$status3 == 1, ], pbc3[pbc3$status3 == 1, ])  long_fit_all <- longitudinalSub(data_fit_all, long_sub_fixed, long_sub_random)  ## 3. Predict event risk for a patient, using only their history up to ##    prediction_time survival_variable_all <- list("Tyears1", "Tyears2", "Tyears3", "Tyears4") survival_trans_function <- list(   fun1 = function(x) abs(x - 1),   fun2 = function(x) abs(x - 3),   fun3 = function(x) abs(x - 5),   fun4 = function(x) abs(x - 7) )  data_raw_predict <- pbc3[pbc3$id == 2 & pbc3$year <= 5, ] data_predict_all <- list(data_raw_predict, data_raw_predict)  risk <- predictRisk(   data_predict_all, long_fit_all, survival_fit_all,   prediction_time = 5, horizon = 1, time_variable = "year",   survival_variable_all, survival_trans_function,   bandcount1 = 10, bandcount2 = 20 ) risk  ## 4. Predict a future biomarker value conditional on survival bio_pred <- predictLongitudinal(   bio_i = 1, data_predict_all, long_fit_all, survival_fit_all,   prediction_time = 5, horizon = 1, time_variable = "year",   survival_variable_all, survival_trans_function,   bandcount2 = 20, bandcount3 = 50 ) bio_pred$Y_predict

title: Reshape recurrent-event data into gap-time episodes for the backward joint model — buildRecurrentEpisodes
code: ## A minimal example: reshaping alone (no model fitting). ## Subject 1: two recurrences, then a terminal event; subject 2: censored. data_events <- data.frame(   id     = c(1, 1, 1, 2),   time   = c(1.2, 2.5, 4.0, 3.1),   status = c(1,   1,   2,   0),   age    = c(58,  58,  58,  61) ) episodes <- buildRecurrentEpisodes(data_events) episodes$episode_data #>   id episode episode_id gap event_any event_type age #> 1  1       1        1:1 1.2         1          0  58 #> 2  1       2        1:2 1.3         1          0  58 #> 3  1       3        1:3 1.5         1          1  58 #> 4  2       1        2:1 3.1         0         NA  61  ## Hospitalizations: each episode starts at DISCHARGE, not at the readmission. ## `time` = readmission (or death/censoring) day; `discharge` = day the stay ## it started ends. Labs drawn in the stay (and before the index discharge at ## day 0) are kept with negative time_in_episode via lookback = Inf. events <- data.frame(id = 1, time = c(20, 60, 90), status = c(1, 1, 0),                      discharge = c(26, 66, NA)) labs <- data.frame(id = 1, day = c(-3, 0, 5, 21, 26, 40, 61, 66, 80)) hf <- buildRecurrentEpisodes(events, labs, time_variable_long = "day",                              restart_variable = "discharge", lookback = Inf) hf$episode_data   # gaps measured from each discharge: 20, 34, 24 #>   id episode episode_id gap event_any event_type #> 1  1       1        1:1  20         1          0 #> 2  1       2        1:2  34         1          0 #> 3  1       3        1:3  24         0         NA hf$long_data[, c("day", "episode", "time_in_episode", "gap")] #>   day episode time_in_episode gap #> 1  -3       1              -3  20 #> 2   0       1               0  20 #> 3   5       1               5  20 #> 4  21       2              -5  34 #> 5  26       2               0  34 #> 6  40       2              14  34 #> 7  61       3              -5  NA #> 8  66       3               0  NA #> 9  80       3              14  NA  # \donttest{ ## A full pipeline on simulated recurrent-event + longitudinal data: ## build episodes -> survivalSub() -> longitudinalSub() -> predictRisk() and ## predictRecurrentCount(). set.seed(1) n <- 60 data_events <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(id) {   k <- sample(1:3, 1)   gaps <- rexp(k, rate = 1)   data.frame(     id = id, time = cumsum(gaps),     status = c(rep(1, k - 1), sample(c(0, 2), 1, prob = c(0.6, 0.4))),     age = round(50 + stats::rnorm(1, sd = 8)), sex = id %% 2   ) }))  ## subject 9999 is still at risk right now, 0.7 time units into their ## 2nd episode (1 prior recurrence, no resolution yet) -- this is who ## we will predict for below. data_events <- rbind(data_events, data.frame(   id = 9999, time = c(0.8, 1.6), status = c(1, 0), age = 55, sex = 1 ))  data_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(seq_len(n), 9999), function(id) {   maxt <- max(data_events$time[data_events$id == id]) + 0.2   tt <- seq(0, maxt, by = 0.25)   data.frame(id = id, year = tt, biomarker = rnorm(length(tt))) }))  built <- buildRecurrentEpisodes(data_events, data_long, time_variable_long = "year") #> buildRecurrentEpisodes(): dropped 50 row(s) of `data_long` whose year fell outside every modeled episode (before time 0 or the `lookback` window, inside a hospital stay not covered by `lookback`, or after the subject's recurrent-event process had already ended).  ## gap-time recurrence hazard + recurrence-vs-terminal-event type model survival_fit_recur <- survivalSub(   built$episode_data,   Surv(gap, event_any) ~ age + sex + episode,   event_type ~ gap + age + sex + episode )  ## longitudinal sub-model, trained on completed episodes only, with the ## random effects grouped by episode (see Details) long_fit_recur <- longitudinalSub(   built$long_data[built$long_data$event_any == 1, ],   biomarker ~ time_in_episode + age + sex + gap + gap * time_in_episode,   ~ time_in_episode | episode_id )  ## subject 9999's open episode: its gap is NA, which predictRisk() reads as ## "still at risk" -- nothing to override open <- built$long_data[built$long_data$id == 9999 & built$long_data$event_any == 0, ] landmark <- max(open$time_in_episode)  ## the risk that their *next* event, within 1 time unit, is a recurrence / ## a terminal event risk <- predictRisk(   open, long_fit_recur, survival_fit_recur,   prediction_time = landmark, horizon = 1, time_variable = "time_in_episode",   survival_variable_all = list(), survival_trans_function = list(),   bandcount1 = 10, bandcount2 = 10 ) risk$risk_prob_1 # P(next event within horizon is a recurrence) #>    9999:2  #> 0.2978591  risk$risk_prob_2 # P(next event within horizon is the terminal event) #>    9999:2  #> 0.2763965   ## the number of recurrences over the next 3 time units predictRecurrentCount(   open, long_fit_recur, survival_fit_recur,   prediction_time = landmark, horizon = 3, time_variable = "time_in_episode",   n_sim = 100, seed = 1 ) #> Predicted recurrences in (0.7, 3.7], 1 patient(s), 100 simulated paths each #> mean expected count 0.470; P(>=1) 0.380; P(>=2) 0.080; P(death) 0.890 #>  #>  episode_id mean_count p_count_0 p_count_1 p_count_2 p_count_3plus p_ge1 p_ge2 #>      9999:2       0.47      0.62       0.3      0.07          0.01  0.38  0.08 #>  p_death #>     0.89 # }

code: # \donttest{ # simulated study: visits every 1-3 years, an event known only to lie # between the last visit without it (L) and the first visit with it (R) set.seed(1) n <- 60 x <- rnorm(n) event_time <- (-log(runif(n)) / (0.05 * exp(0.5 * x)))^(1 / 1.5) surv <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n), x = x, L = NA_real_, R = NA_real_) long <- list() for (i in seq_len(n)) {   visits <- c(0, cumsum(runif(30, 1, 3)))   visits <- visits[visits < 12]   if (event_time[i] > max(visits)) {     surv$L[i] <- max(visits)     seen <- visits   } else {     k <- findInterval(event_time[i], visits)     surv$L[i] <- visits[k]     surv$R[i] <- visits[k + 1]     seen <- visits[visits <= event_time[i]]   }   long[[i]] <- data.frame(id = i, year = seen, x = x[i],                           y = 1 + 0.3 * seen - 0.2 * event_time[i] + 0.4 * x[i] +                             rnorm(1, 0, 0.5) + rnorm(length(seen), 0, 0.3)) } long <- do.call(rbind, long)  fit <- fitIntervalBJM(surv, long, Surv(L, R, type = "interval2") ~ x,                       event_time = "Tev", long_sub_fixed = y ~ year + Tev + x,                       long_sub_random = ~ year | id, time_variable = "year",                       n_burnin = 2, n_imputations = 2, n_thin = 1, n_grid = 15,                       seed = 1) fit$pooled #>  #> Call: #> poolLongitudinalSub(m = 2 completed-data fits, M = 1 longitudinal outcome) #>  #> ================================================================= #>  Rubin's-Rules-Pooled Longitudinal Sub-model(s) #> ----------------------------------------------------------------- #>  [1] Outcome 1 #>  #>                Value       SE    DF      t  p-value     #> (Intercept)  0.85680  0.19666 36.31  4.357 0.000104 *** #> year         0.29168  0.01648 92.54 17.696  < 2e-16 *** #> Tev         -0.16460  0.03693 20.72 -4.458 0.000224 *** #> x            0.38435  0.09815 45.43  3.916 0.000300 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #>   Fraction of missing information (FMI), by coefficient: #>   (Intercept) = 0.169,  year = 0.033,  Tev = 0.222,  x = 0.051  #>  #> =================================================================  # the fit plugs into the prediction functions; Tev is unknown for a new patient history <- long[long$id == 1 & long$year <= 2, ] history$Tev <- NA_real_ predictRisk(history, fit$long_fit_all, fit$survival_fit_all,             prediction_time = 2, horizon = 2, time_variable = "year",             survival_variable_all = NULL, survival_trans_function = NULL,             bandcount1 = 10, bandcount2 = 20) #>  #> ================================================================= #>  Dynamic Prediction - Event Risk #> ----------------------------------------------------------------- #>   Competing risks   : No #>   Subjects          : 1 #> ----------------------------------------------------------------- #>  #>  Subject Risk Prob Already, undetected #>        1    0.3007               0.592 #>  #>   Interval-censored: risks condition on being event-free at each subject's #>  last visit; 'Already, undetected' is the probability the event happened #>  between that visit and the prediction time. #>  #> ================================================================= #>  # }

code: # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("torch", quietly = TRUE) && torch::torch_is_installed()) {   data(pbc3)   data_fit_all <- pbc3[pbc3$status3 == 1, ]    # pbc3's complete-case subset has no missing serBilir/albumin values;   # artificially delete some at random (MCAR, a special case of MAR) to   # simulate the interrupted-follow-up gaps imputeLongitudinal() targets   set.seed(1)   n <- nrow(data_fit_all)   data_fit_all$serBilir[sample.int(n, floor(0.1 * n))] <- NA   data_fit_all$albumin[sample.int(n, floor(0.1 * n))] <- NA    long_sub_fixed <- list(     "long1" = serBilir ~ year + age + sex + years,     "long2" = albumin ~ year + age + sex + years)   long_sub_random <- list("long1" = ~ year | id, "long2" = ~ year | id)    imputed <- imputeLongitudinal(data_fit_all, long_sub_fixed,                                  long_sub_random, time_variable = "year",                                  epochs = 50, seed = 1)   long_fit_all <- longitudinalSub(imputed$data_fit_all, long_sub_fixed,                                    long_sub_random)    # the diffusion backend fills the same gaps via a conditional DDPM   # instead of a VAE -- same call shape, just a different `method`   imputed_diffusion <- imputeLongitudinal(data_fit_all, long_sub_fixed,                                            long_sub_random, time_variable = "year",                                            method = "diffusion", epochs = 50,                                            diffusion_steps = 30, seed = 1) } # }

code: # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("torch", quietly = TRUE) && torch::torch_is_installed()) {   data(pbc3)   data_fit_all <- pbc3[pbc3$status3 == 1, ]    set.seed(1)   n <- nrow(data_fit_all)   data_fit_all$serBilir[sample.int(n, floor(0.1 * n))] <- NA   data_fit_all$albumin[sample.int(n, floor(0.1 * n))] <- NA    long_sub_fixed <- list(     "long1" = serBilir ~ year + age + sex + years,     "long2" = albumin ~ year + age + sex + years)   long_sub_random <- list("long1" = ~ year | id, "long2" = ~ year | id)    imputed <- imputeLongitudinal(data_fit_all, long_sub_fixed, long_sub_random,                                  time_variable = "year", n_imputations = 5,                                  impute = "multiple", epochs = 50, seed = 1)    long_fit_all_list <- lapply(imputed$data_fit_all_list, function(d) {     longitudinalSub(d, long_sub_fixed, long_sub_random)   })   pooled <- poolLongitudinalSub(long_fit_all_list)   pooled } # }
